# files_child_site_management_policy (Resource)

A Child Site Management Policy is a centralized policy defined by a parent site to enforce consistent configurations across child sites. These policies allow parent sites to maintain control over specific aspects of their child sites' functionality and appearance.

Non-default policies apply only to the child sites listed in `child_site_ids`, and each child site can be explicitly assigned to only one policy.

One policy can be designated as the default policy. It applies to every child site not explicitly assigned to another policy or listed in its `skip_child_site_ids`, including newly created child sites. Only a default policy can exclude child sites. The `value` field contains the policy configuration data, with the format varying based on the policy type. When a policy is active, its managed configurations are automatically enforced on applicable child sites, and attribute modifications are not permitted.

On a Child Site, listing policies returns only the policy covering that site. Each key in `value` identifies a managed setting, but its value is always `null`. Read non-secret effective setting values from the Child Site's own Site settings response.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "files_child_site_management_policy" "example_child_site_management_policy" {
  value               = {
    color2_left      = "#000000"
    folder_behaviors = [
      {
        file_expiration = {
          value = {
            days_to_retain = 30
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
  skip_child_site_ids = [1, 2]
  child_site_ids      = [1, 2]
  default_policy      = true
  policy_type         = "settings"
  name                = "example"
  description         = "example"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `policy_type` (String) Type of policy.  Valid values: `settings`.

### Optional

- `child_site_ids` (List of Number) IDs of child sites explicitly assigned to this non-default policy.
- `default_policy` (Boolean) Whether this policy applies to child sites not explicitly assigned to another policy.
- `description` (String) Description for this policy.
- `name` (String) Name for this policy.
- `skip_child_site_ids` (List of Number) IDs of child sites excluded from this default policy.
- `value` (Dynamic, Sensitive) Policy configuration data. On a Child Site, contains only managed setting names with null values. Settings policies accept site settings plus an optional `folder_behaviors` array for parent-managed root behaviors on child sites. For more information, refer to the Value Hash section of the developer documentation.

### Read-Only

- `applied_child_site_ids` (List of Number) IDs of child sites that this policy has been applied to. This field is read-only.
- `created_at` (String) When this policy was created.
- `id` (Number) Policy ID.
- `updated_at` (String) When this policy was last updated.

### JSON property details

These properties will move from Dynamic to typed schemas in a major provider release planned for March 1, 2027. Until then, JSON-encoded configuration remains supported with a deprecation warning.

#### value

Site settings and root folder behaviors that a settings policy manages on applicable Child Sites. On the parent site, values follow the same validation as Site settings and Behaviors, so a setting can be null only where that Site setting accepts null. Older policies may hold boolean and integer settings as strings, such as `"false"` or `"30"`. Child sites receive the converted value. Unsupported keys are removed when the policy is saved. When policies are listed from a Child Site, the values are hidden: each managed key is present with a null value, whatever its type on the parent site.

- `domain_letsencrypt_chain` (string, optional) Letsencrypt chain to use when registering SSL Certificate for domain. No longer used as of 2026.

- `office_integration_available` (boolean, optional) If true, allows users to use a document editing integration.
- `office_integration_type` (string, optional) Which document editing integration to support. Files.com Editor or Microsoft Office for the Web.
- `pin_all_remote_servers_to_site_region` (boolean, optional) If true, we will ensure that all internal communications with any remote server are made through the primary region of the site. This setting overrides individual remote server settings.
- `motd_text` (string, optional) A message to show users when they connect via FTP or SFTP.

- `motd_use_for_sftp` (boolean, optional) Show message to users connecting via SFTP

- `disable_all_ai_features` (boolean, optional) If true, all AI features are disabled for this site.
- `ai_feature_availability` (object, optional) Availability settings for AI features. Each feature requires the site_admins, workspace_admins, folder_admins, and all_users keys. Optional selected_group_members defaults to false; when true, members of at least one group in group_ids get access regardless of the other options. All availability options are additive: any enabled option matching the user grants access. Optional group_ids is an array of integer IDs of active groups on this site, from any workspace. Omitted or empty group_ids grants no access through selected_group_members and does not affect other options. Disabling all AI features overrides these settings.

- `calculate_file_checksums_crc32` (boolean, optional) Calculate CRC32 checksums for files?
- `calculate_file_checksums_md5` (boolean, optional) Calculate MD5 checksums for files?
- `calculate_file_checksums_sha1` (boolean, optional) Calculate SHA1 checksums for files?
- `calculate_file_checksums_sha256` (boolean, optional) Calculate SHA256 checksums for files?
- `migrate_remote_server_sync_to_sync` (boolean, optional) If true, we will migrate all remote server syncs to the new Sync model.
- `as2_message_retention_days` (integer, optional) Number of days to retain AS2 messages (incoming and outgoing).
- `file_activity_events_enabled` (boolean, optional) If true, file operations produce file_action.activity.v1 EventChannel events in all workspaces. Defaults to false; subscription filters and workspace access still control delivery.
- `username_display` (string, optional) How usernames are displayed in the web UI. Can be `username_only`, `full_name_only`, `full_name_username`, `full_name_company`, or `full_name_username_company`.
- `session_expiry_minutes` (integer, optional) Session expiry in minutes
- `ssl_required` (boolean, optional) Is SSL required?  Disabling this is insecure.
- `sftp_insecure_ciphers` (boolean, optional) If true, we will allow weak and known insecure ciphers to be used for SFTP connections.  Enabling this setting severely weakens the security of your site and it is not recommend, except as a last resort for compatibility.
- `sftp_insecure_diffie_hellman` (boolean, optional) If true, we will allow weak Diffie Hellman parameters to be used within ciphers for SFTP that are otherwise on our secure list.  This has the effect of making the cipher weaker than our normal threshold for security, but is required to support certain legacy or broken SSH and MFT clients.  Enabling this weakens security, but not nearly as much as enabling the full `sftp_insecure_ciphers` option.

A certificate-verified STARTTLS connection automatically changes if_available to require unless smtp_ssl is managed by a parent policy. require requires STARTTLS before authentication; require_implicit uses TLS from connection start; never disables TLS. TLS verifies the server certificate against smtp_address. Encryption is never automatically downgraded.

Terraform treats `value` as sensitive because it can hold secrets. A root module output that returns it needs `sensitive = true`.

##### `value.ai_feature_availability`

- `in_app_ai_assistant` (object, required) Options are additive: any enabled option that matches the user grants access. Disabling all AI features overrides these options.

##### `value.ai_feature_availability.in_app_ai_assistant`

- `site_admins` (boolean, required) If true, site admins have access. Null disables the option. Null is accepted until March 1, 2027. The typed schema then requires true or false.
- `workspace_admins` (boolean, required) If true, workspace admins have access. Null disables the option. Null is accepted until March 1, 2027. The typed schema then requires true or false.
- `folder_admins` (boolean, required) If true, folder admins have access. Null disables the option. Null is accepted until March 1, 2027. The typed schema then requires true or false.
- `all_users` (boolean, required) If true, all users have access. Null disables the option. Null is accepted until March 1, 2027. The typed schema then requires true or false.
- `selected_group_members` (boolean, optional) If true, members of at least one group in group_ids have access. Defaults to false. Null disables the option.
- `group_ids` (list of integers, optional) IDs of active groups on this site, from any workspace. Omitted or empty group_ids grants no access through selected_group_members.

##### `value.bundle_watermark_value`

- `transparency` (integer, optional) Percentage applied to the watermark.

- `days_to_retain` (integer, required) Number of days to keep files around.
- `delete_empty_folders` (boolean, optional) If `true`, delete empty folders inside this tree after expired files are removed. Folders with explicit configuration, such as permissions, notifications, or behaviors, are preserved.

- `value` (object, required) Behavior value. Its fields match the value of a Behavior of this type.

##### `value.folder_behaviors[].limit_file_extensions.value`

- `extensions` (list of strings, required) Array of whitelisted/blacklisted file extensions, depending on `mode`.
- `mode` (string, optional) Controls whether the behavior acts as a whitelist or as a blacklist. Default is `whitelist`.

##### `value.folder_behaviors[].limit_file_regex`

- `value` (list of strings, required) Behavior value. Its fields match the value of a Behavior of this type.

#### Migrating JSON-encoded configuration

Replace `jsonencode(...)` with native HCL as in the examples below.

```hcl
# Legacy JSON encoding
value = jsonencode({
  color2_left      = "#000000"
  folder_behaviors = [
    {
      behavior = "file_expiration"
      value    = {
        days_to_retain = 30
      }
    }
  ]
})

# Native HCL. Each folder_behaviors item moves under the name in its behavior field. Both nestings work until March 1, 2027.
value = {
  color2_left      = "#000000"
  folder_behaviors = [
    {
      file_expiration = {
        value = {
          days_to_retain = 30
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Child Site Management Policies can be imported by specifying the id.
terraform import files_child_site_management_policy.example_child_site_management_policy 1
```
